evidence.claim: Colorado DOT presents its succession of environments as a lesson in Rocky Mountain ecosystems and lists a one-hour drive over 22 miles.

evidence.claim: At its northern end, Georgetown began during the 1859 gold rush; the discovery of silver in 1864 started the local silver boom.
evidence.quote: Gold was discovered in Georgetown by George and David Griffiths in 1859, and Georgetown eventually took its name from the former. The gold finds in the area were relatively minor, but a major lode of silver was discovered in 1864, kicking off the local boom.

evidence.claim: The pass received its name in 1953, honoring Byron Guanella, a Clear Creek County road supervisor and commissioner for nearly 50 years.
evidence.quote: The pass was named in 1953 for Byron Guanella, a road supervisor and commissioner in Clear Creek County for nearly 50 years.

evidence.claim: From Georgetown in the Clear Creek valley, the road heads south to the pass, then descends toward Grant in the Geneva Creek valley.
evidence.quote: The pass provides a route between Georgetown in the valley of Clear Creek to the north and Grant in the valley of Geneva Creek, a tributary of the North Fork South Platte River, to the south.

evidence.claim: The route is paved all the way to U.S. 285.
evidence.quote: The entire route from Georgetown to U.S. Highway 285 is paved

evidence.claim: At the crest, trails branch east toward Mount Bierstadt and west toward Square Top Mountain.
evidence.quote: At the summit of the pass, hiking trails lead east to Mount Bierstadt (elevation 14,060 ft (4,290 m)) and west to Square Top Mountain

evidence.claim: The southern end reaches Grant at the mouth of Geneva Creek, where the creek joins the North Fork South Platte.
evidence.quote: It joins the North Fork South Platte from the north at Grant along U.S. Highway 285.

evidence.claim: Georgetown began with gold, but silver gave the town its mining boom.
evidence.quote: The gold finds in the area were relatively minor, but a major lode of silver was discovered in 1864, kicking off the local boom.

evidence.claim: Gold was discovered here in 1859; the larger silver discovery followed in 1864.
evidence.quote: Gold was discovered in Georgetown by George and David Griffiths in 1859, and Georgetown eventually took its name from the former. The gold finds in the area were relatively minor, but a major lode of silver was discovered in 1864

evidence.claim: Georgetown became a center for thousands of miners working the surrounding hills.
evidence.quote: Georgetown became a center for thousands of miners operating in the surrounding hills.

evidence.claim: The town stretches along Clear Creek, with its historic downtown at the southern, upper end.
evidence.quote: The town stretches roughly north–south along Clear Creek, hemmed in by the mountains, with the historic downtown located at the southern (upper) end

evidence.claim: Preserved buildings from the silver boom belong to a National Historic Landmark district that also includes Silver Plume and the railroad park between the two towns.
evidence.quote: The Georgetown–Silver Plume National Historic Landmark District is a federally designated United States National Historic Landmark that comprises the Town of Georgetown, the Town of Silver Plume, and the Georgetown Loop Historic Mining & Railroad Park

evidence.claim: The district preserves mining structures as well as town buildings.
evidence.quote: The district includes well-preserved examples of the buildings and mining structures of the Colorado Silver Boom from 1864 to 1893.

evidence.claim: The road reaches open tundra above timberline at Guanella Pass.
evidence.quote: The road crests well above timberline, where every spring the grasses and flowers stubbornly renew, and the fragile tundra thaws and blossoms.

evidence.claim: Below the crest, streams wind through broad meadows; lower still, spruce, fir, aspen and pine grow along cascading creeks.
evidence.quote: The lower elevations are green and wet, thick stands of spruce, fir, aspen, and pine rising along cascading creeks. Higher up, the streams snake through broad meadows

evidence.claim: Trails leave the summit eastward for Mount Bierstadt and westward for Square Top Mountain.
evidence.quote: At the summit of the pass, hiking trails lead east to Mount Bierstadt (elevation 14,060 ft (4,290 m)) and west to Square Top Mountain

evidence.claim: Bierstadt takes its name from German-American landscape painter Albert Bierstadt, who made the first recorded ascent in 1863.
evidence.quote: It was named in honor of Albert Bierstadt, a German-American landscape painter who made the first recorded summit of the mountain in 1863.

evidence.claim: Its trail first descends into the marshlands of Scott Gomer Creek before climbing the mountain’s western slopes.
evidence.quote: The trail descends slightly into the fairly level marshlands surrounding Scott Gomer Creek before reaching Bierstadt's western slopes.

evidence.claim: The road closes seasonally on or about November 26 and reopens Memorial Day weekend, with closure points at Naylor Lake and Burning Bear Campground.
evidence.quote: Guanella Pass Road is seasonally closed on or about Nov. 26, and reopens on Memorial Day weekend at Naylor Lake on the Clear Creek County side and Burning Bear Campground on the Park County side.

evidence.claim: Geneva Creek reaches the North Fork South Platte at Grant, beside U.S. 285.
evidence.quote: It joins the North Fork South Platte from the north at Grant along U.S. Highway 285.

evidence.claim: The creek rises at the Continental Divide west of Mount Bierstadt and descends southeast through a canyon.
evidence.quote: It rises at the continental divide west of Mount Bierstadt and descends through a canyon to the southeast.

evidence.claim: Its valley carries the byway toward this southern junction.
evidence.quote: The valley of the river provides the route of the Guanella Pass Scenic Byway between Georgetown and Grant.

evidence.claim: Grant is an unincorporated community in the Front Range foothills, with a retired general store, post office, houses and trailers between the highway and river.
evidence.quote: It consists largely of a retired general store, post office, and surrounding houses and trailers along the south side of the highway and along the north side of the river.

evidence.claim: County Road 62 follows Geneva Creek north from here toward the pass and Georgetown.
evidence.quote: County Road 62 follows the creek northward to Guanella Pass, leading to Georgetown in the canyon of Clear Creek.
